pages.raw_meta: Bridger Aerospace delivers aerial firefighting, air attack coordination, and real-time wildfire intelligence using advanced aircraft, multi-mission operations, and the IGNIS platform for safer, more effective wildfire response.
raw_blocks: AERIAL FIREFIGHTING & SPECIAL MISSIONS

“Wildfires are now a year-round threat. At Bridger, our team works tirelessly to stay prepared for when the next call comes in. A decade ago, we started out with a single plane. Today, we operate a world-class fleet of specialized aircraft to gather real-time data on wildfires, map them out, and extinguish them. We are proud to provide air support for firefighters on the ground, and to do our part in protecting lives, property, and the environment from wildfires.”
Sam Davis – President and CEO
To protect lives, property, critical infrastructure, and the environment from wildfires and beyond.

To set the standard for safety and effectiveness in aerial firefighting, to innovate and deploy the most advanced technology in our industry, and to maximize shareholder value through expanding our contracts, optimizing our fleet, and forming new strategic partnerships.

Bridger Aerospace provides disaster response through aerial firefighting , special-mission aviation and wildland firefighting technology, supported by in-house engineering and MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul) services. Its operations include initial attack fire suppression , multi-mission mapping and intelligence, air attack coordination , and real-time data delivery through the IGNIS platform to support wildfire and natural disaster response.

Aerial firefighting is the use of specialized aircraft to support wildfire management, containment, and suppression by delivering water or retardant, providing real-time intelligence and mapping , coordinating airspace through Air Attack, and supporting ground firefighters during active incidents.

Bridger Aerospace ensures safety and compliance through FAA-certified operations, adherence to USFS and DOI standards, rigorous pilot training, standardized operating procedures, and in-house maintenance and engineering programs designed to support high-risk aviation missions.

The Bridger Aerospace fleet includes CL-415EAF and CL-215T Super Scooper amphibious firefighting aircraft, along with Pilatus PC-12 and Daher Kodiak aircraft configured for air attack (aerial supervision) and Multi-Mission intelligence, mapping, and detection operations

IGNIS is Bridger Aerospace’s wildfire technology platform that provides a common operating picture for wildland firefighters. It enables teams to share intelligence, stay up to date on evolving incidents, and access aircraft livestreams and the latest aviation map products. IGNIS supports offline data sharing, air-to-ground integration, wildfire-specific map layers, and fire weather updates, helping firefighters, incident management teams, and agencies coordinate more effectively during active wildfire operations.

Air Attack is the airborne command function over a wildfire, where an Air Tactical Group Supervisor (ATGS) coordinates firefighting aircraft, manages airspace, and aligns aerial tactics with ground operations to improve firefighter safety and overall wildfire suppression effectiveness.
Bridger Aerospace conducts aerial firefighting operations across the United States and Canada, supporting federal, state, provincial, and local agencies during wildfire operations.

Aerial firefighting is a critical component of wildfire management, supporting ground-based suppression and firefighter safety. It is incredibly effective when used early and in close coordination with ground crews, where rapid, high-volume suppression can slow fire spread, reduce fire intensity, and increase the likelihood of containment before fires become large, complex incidents. Even during extended incidents, aerial firefighting remains essential for protecting firefighters, supporting suppression efforts, and enabling effective incident management.

raw_blocks: Our mission is simple: To protect lives, property, critical infrastructure, and the environment from wildfires and beyond.

Bridger Aerospace is a mission-driven organization fueled by the purpose to modernize and strengthen how wildfires are fought. Through the curation of aviation, technology, and engineering, Bridger is a leader in fighting wildfires – from detection to suppression.

Bridger Aerospace deploys the most advanced technologies in aviation to protect lives, property, critical infrastructure, and the environment, delivering these capabilities where they matter most, from wildfire response to defense and beyond.

Bridger Aerospace is a publicly traded aerial firefighting and aerospace services company headquartered in Belgrade, Montana, at Bozeman Yellowstone International Airport (KBZN), with a secondary headquarters in Huntsville, Alabama. Founded in 2014, the company has grown from a single aircraft operation into a leading provider of aerial firefighting, operational intelligence, and specialized aviation services supporting government agencies and emergency response partners across the world.

Founded by combat veterans to bring the principles of close air support to wildland firefighting. Bridger began with a single aircraft in Montana with a mission to improve aerial support for firefighters protecting communities.
Bridger’s first year supporting wildfire response, flying three Twin Commander aircraft in the Air Attack role and establishing the operational foundation for future aerial firefighting operations.
Bridger acquired its first two CL-415EAF Super Scoopers , expanding into aerial fire suppression and rapid initial attack.
The fleet grew to four Super Scoopers and 20 total aircraft , dropping more than 5 million gallons of water during the fire season.
Bridger added its fifth Super Scooper and introduced the Pilatus PC-12 to modernize Air Attack and aerial intelligence operations.
Bridger became publicly traded on NASDAQ (BAER) , added its sixth Scooper , completed a third hangar , acquired IGNIS , and began building PC-12 Multi-Mission Aircraft .
Bridger acquired FMS Aerospace , adding aircraft engineering, modification, flight testing, and certification capabilities while supporting early-season wildfire deployments in Texas and Oklahoma.
Bridger executed the earliest deployment in company history to California and secured a State of Alaska firefighting contract , expanding operational coverage across North America.
Sam Davis President and CEO
Anne Hayes Chief Financial Officer
Bill Andrews Chief Operating Officer
Rob Mauracher EVP of Commercial Strategy
Justin Mogford General Counsel and Corporate Secretary
Mission Readiness Begins with Trusted Support
We deliver reliable flight operations, integrated technology, engineering expertise, and MRO support that federal, state, and industry partners depend on.

raw_blocks: A Field-First Common Operating Picture for Emergency Response
Built by firefighters for firefighters.
ALREADY A MEMBER? LOG IN
Incidents Move Faster Than Static Tools

PDF maps, printed Incident Action Plans, delayed imagery, and disconnected software create gaps in awareness. IGNIS replaces static maps with a live operating picture, built by those actively managing the fire.
IOS | ANDROID | WEB
IGNIS provides real-time situational awareness that helps firefighters and incident managers make better, risk-informed decisions in the field.
Dozer lines and hand lines
Built for Firefighters in the Field
Crews can join an incident ahead of time with an incident code or link, or on scene using a QR code.
Incoming resources can access the full incident map and operational data before arriving on scene, helping crews arrive informed and ready to operate.
Firefighters in the field can contribute directly to the operational map.
Teams can easily add locations for:
This allows the map to reflect the real conditions crews are seeing on the ground.
Wildfires rarely occur where connectivity is reliable. IGNIS allows devices to share updates even when service is unavailable.
Using a Bluetooth mesh network, devices automatically exchange new information such as fire features and perimeter updates. When one device reconnects to service, it synchronizes the entire network.
This keeps teams working with the most current information available, even in remote terrain.
IGNIS also serves as a hub for the latest incident data.
Firefighters can quickly upload and access:
This ensures the entire team is operating from the same source of information.
IGNIS connects aerial intelligence directly to the incident map, allowing command teams and firefighters to see the fire from the air in real time.
Real-time aircraft position and track
Drop target coordination for air attack and suppression aircraft
IGNIS provides a 3D operating environment that helps teams understand terrain and operational features quickly.
Layered operational data including perimeters and fire lines
This allows teams to maintain a clear operating picture, even when aircraft are not overhead.
Two ways to get IGNIS
Free on iOS & Android
Everything you need to stay field-ready: PDF maps in 3D, fire symbology, offline maps, and fire weather forecasts. Plus the ability to join any incident you’re invited to.

The full operating picture: Manage incidents, invite resources to the live operational map via QR code, view live personnel locations, and see the fire in real time from the air when Bridger aircraft are assigned.
Joining an incident is free for anyone with an invite. Creating and managing an incident requires IGNIS Pro.
Offline base layers with auto-sync
PDF Map Overlays in 3D
Fire-specific symbology & track recording
Pre-attack materials & custom org layers
Incidents — create, collaborate & invite via QR code
Teams — organize people & share content
Personnel Location — live sharing for incidents
Live Bridger aerial video on the map
The Only COP Built for Advanced Aerial Intelligence

IGNIS is designed to integrate directly with multi-mission aircraft equipped with advanced sensor systems. These aircraft can provide real-time imagery, video, and intelligence directly into the operational map.
Aircraft position and flight path
Sensor field-of-view across the terrain
This allows crews to see the current fire behavior and operational conditions from the air as they happen.
Available with IGNIS PRO when Bridger Aircraft are Assigned.

IGNIS allows resources to mark aircraft drop targets directly on the operational map. Aerial resources can reference the same map, reducing time spent identifying targets over the radio and informing aviation crews before they launch.
This helps air and ground teams coordinate faster and deliver water or retardant drops more efficiently.
Built for the Way Incidents Actually Scale
Wildfires are dynamic and conditions can change rapidly. IGNIS is built to scale with them.
Crews can join instantly using QR codes
Incoming resources can view the full incident map before arrival
Data continuously updates as the incident evolves
From Initial Attack through Suppression Repair, IGNIS maintains a shared operational picture for the entire team.

REAL-TIME INTEL, BUILT FOR THE FIELD
